newsitem.title: FRANCE: French train conductors defy unions, extend strike.
newsitem.headline: French train conductors defy unions, extend strike.

text.p: Most of France's striking train conductors voted to extend their three-day-old protest into Saturday, defying unions and threatening to ruin the long Pentecost weekend for thousands of holidaymakers.
Although several unions said they had made significant gains in all-night negotiations with the SNCF state railway company, conductors in most regions decided to stay off work.

The state railway company SNCF, which had earlier said there was a move towards returning to work, said traffic disruptions were continuing although it was doing all it could to cope with the rush of holidaymakers.

The strike has cut services by about a third on high-speed TGV and regional lines across France, but has spared high-speed trains between Paris and Brussels and Eurostar trains connecting London to Paris and Brussels through the Channel tunnel.
Trains cannot run without conductors, who are responsible for safety as well as checking tickets.
"We obtained significant advances," said Bruno Dalberto, head of the pro-Socialist CFDT rail union after overnight talks ended at about 5 a.m. (0300 GMT).
But the hardline Sud-Rail union said they fell far short of demands.

SNCF agreed to promote an extra 860 of the current 10,000 conductors and hire 200 more this year as well as raise their monthly bonus to 900 francs ($155) from 700 francs ($120) by year-end and to 1,000 francs ($170) early next year.
The conductors staged a similar strike last month in another sign of opposition to austerity policies of the centre-right government of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
